=== SIGNOZ QUERY BUILDER V5 — TRACES GUIDE ===

== FILTER EXPRESSION FORMAT ==

Filters are a STRING expression in filter.expression — NOT a structured {op, items} object.

CORRECT:   "filter": {"expression": "has_error = true AND k8s.namespace.name = 'my-ns'"}
INCORRECT: "filter": {"op": "AND", "items": [...]}

Operators: =  !=  >  >=  <  <=  IN  NOT IN  LIKE  NOT LIKE  ILIKE  NOT ILIKE  CONTAINS  NOT CONTAINS  REGEXP  NOT REGEXP  BETWEEN  NOT BETWEEN  EXISTS  NOT EXISTS
Combine:   AND  OR  (use parentheses for precedence)

Examples:
  has_error = true
  duration_nano > 500000000
  status_code_string = 'Error'
  name LIKE '%payment%'
  has_error = true AND k8s.namespace.name = 'prod'
  (has_error = true OR duration_nano > 1000000000) AND service.name = 'checkout'

== FIELD DISCOVERY ==

Unknown keys hard-error. Built-in span columns are stable, but resource and span/tag attributes depend
on this workspace's instrumentation. Do not guess unfamiliar field names. Discover keys, then confirm
their observed values before filtering:
  signoz_get_field_keys(signal="traces", fieldContext="span")
  signoz_get_field_keys(signal="traces", fieldContext="resource")
  signoz_get_field_keys(signal="traces", fieldContext="attribute")
  signoz_get_field_values(signal="traces", name="<field>", fieldContext="<matching context>")

The fieldContext value "tag" is accepted as an alias for "attribute" by the discovery tools; Query
Builder selectFields and groupBy use "tag". The resource and tag names below are common examples, not
a complete catalog for every workspace.

== FIELD NAMES — THREE CATEGORIES ==

--- 1. Built-in span columns (snake_case, fieldContext: "span") ---

Use these directly by name in filter expressions. In selectFields, use fieldContext "span"
to make the built-in/span-column intent explicit:

  has_error            bool      — whether the span has an error
  status_message       string    — OTel status message
  status_code_string   string    — span status: 'Ok', 'Error', or 'Unset' (prefer has_error = true for errors)
  status_code          number    — numeric OTel status code
  duration_nano        number    — span duration in nanoseconds
  trace_id             string    — trace identifier
  span_id              string    — span identifier
  parent_span_id       string    — parent span identifier
  name                 string    — span/operation name
  timestamp            number    — span start timestamp
  http_method          string    — HTTP method
  http_url             string    — HTTP URL
  kind_string          string    — 'Server', 'Client', 'Internal', 'Producer', 'Consumer'
  response_status_code string    — HTTP response status as string; do not use for numeric comparisons

For numeric HTTP status comparisons, use a numeric span/tag attribute such as
attribute.http.response.status_code after verifying it exists for your data.

selectFields entry:
  {"name": "has_error", "fieldDataType": "bool", "signal": "traces", "fieldContext": "span"}
  {"name": "duration_nano", "fieldDataType": "number", "signal": "traces", "fieldContext": "span"}
  {"name": "name", "fieldDataType": "string", "signal": "traces", "fieldContext": "span"}

--- 2. Resource attributes (dot notation, fieldContext: "resource") ---

OTel resource attributes set by the SDK/collector on the originating entity:

  service.name              string — service name
  k8s.namespace.name        string — Kubernetes namespace
  k8s.pod.name              string — Kubernetes pod name
  k8s.node.name             string — Kubernetes node name
  k8s.cluster.name          string — Kubernetes cluster name
  signoz.deployment.tier    string — custom deployment tier tag
  host.name                 string — host name

selectFields entry (fieldContext: "resource" required):
  {"name": "service.name", "fieldDataType": "string", "signal": "traces", "fieldContext": "resource"}
  {"name": "k8s.namespace.name", "fieldDataType": "string", "signal": "traces", "fieldContext": "resource"}

--- 3. Span/tag attributes (dot notation, fieldContext: "tag") ---

OTel span attributes set per-span:

  http.response.status_code number — HTTP status code attribute
  db.system          string — database system (e.g. "postgresql")
  db.operation       string — database operation
  rpc.method         string — RPC method name
  messaging.system   string — messaging system (e.g. "kafka")

selectFields entry (fieldContext: "tag" required):
  {"name": "http.response.status_code", "fieldDataType": "number", "signal": "traces", "fieldContext": "tag"}

== RESULT BOUNDS AND ORDERING ==

Every builder_query must include a positive limit and explicit order.

  raw / trace: limit 100; order by timestamp desc
  scalar:      limit 100 groups; order by the primary aggregation desc unless the task needs another order
  time_series: limit 100 groups; order by the primary aggregation desc unless the task needs another order

For time_series queries with groupBy, the limit selects top groups using the ordering across the ENTIRE
time range, not each time bucket. A short-lived spike can fall outside the selected groups. Use an explicit
smaller limit only when the user asks for top N; use a larger limit when completeness
matters more than response size.

== COMPLETE WORKING EXAMPLES ==

--- Example 1: Raw error spans (requestType: "raw") ---

{
  "schemaVersion": "v1",
  "start": 1756386047000,
  "end": 1756387847000,
  "requestType": "raw",
  "compositeQuery": {
    "queries": [
      {
        "type": "builder_query",
        "spec": {
          "name": "A",
          "signal": "traces",
          "disabled": false,
          "limit": 100,
          "offset": 0,
          "order": [{"key": {"name": "timestamp"}, "direction": "desc"}],
          "having": {"expression": ""},
          "filter": {"expression": "has_error = true AND k8s.namespace.name = 'prod'"},
          "selectFields": [
            {"name": "service.name", "fieldDataType": "string", "signal": "traces", "fieldContext": "resource"},
            {"name": "name",          "fieldDataType": "string", "signal": "traces", "fieldContext": "span"},
            {"name": "has_error",     "fieldDataType": "bool",   "signal": "traces", "fieldContext": "span"},
            {"name": "duration_nano", "fieldDataType": "number", "signal": "traces", "fieldContext": "span"},
            {"name": "status_message","fieldDataType": "string", "signal": "traces", "fieldContext": "span"},
            {"name": "trace_id",      "fieldDataType": "string", "signal": "traces", "fieldContext": "span"},
            {"name": "span_id",       "fieldDataType": "string", "signal": "traces", "fieldContext": "span"}
          ]
        }
      }
    ]
  },
  "formatOptions": {"formatTableResultForUI": false, "fillGaps": false},
  "variables": {}
}

--- Example 2: Aggregation query — error count grouped by service (requestType: "scalar") ---

{
  "schemaVersion": "v1",
  "start": 1756386047000,
  "end": 1756387847000,
  "requestType": "scalar",
  "compositeQuery": {
    "queries": [
      {
        "type": "builder_query",
        "spec": {
          "name": "A",
          "signal": "traces",
          "disabled": false,
          "limit": 100,
          "offset": 0,
          "having": {"expression": ""},
          "filter": {"expression": "has_error = true"},
          "aggregations": [
            {"expression": "count()"}
          ],
          "groupBy": [
            {"name": "service.name", "fieldDataType": "string", "signal": "traces", "fieldContext": "resource"}
          ],
          "order": [{"key": {"name": "count()"}, "direction": "desc"}]
        }
      }
    ]
  },
  "formatOptions": {"formatTableResultForUI": false, "fillGaps": false},
  "variables": {}
}

--- Example 3: Time series — P99 latency over time (requestType: "time_series") ---

{
  "schemaVersion": "v1",
  "start": 1756386047000,
  "end": 1756387847000,
  "requestType": "time_series",
  "compositeQuery": {
    "queries": [
      {
        "type": "builder_query",
        "spec": {
          "name": "A",
          "signal": "traces",
          "disabled": false,
          "stepInterval": 60,
          "limit": 100,
          "offset": 0,
          "order": [{"key": {"name": "p99(duration_nano)"}, "direction": "desc"}],
          "having": {"expression": ""},
          "filter": {"expression": "service.name = 'checkout'"},
          "aggregations": [
            {"expression": "p99(duration_nano)"}
          ]
        }
      }
    ]
  },
  "formatOptions": {"formatTableResultForUI": false, "fillGaps": false},
  "variables": {}
}

== TIMESTAMP FORMAT ==

The top-level "start" and "end" request fields are Unix milliseconds (13-digit), e.g. 1756386047000.
Prefer start/end to bound the time window. The built-in "timestamp" COLUMN is nanosecond-scale
(DateTime64(9)), so do NOT put a millisecond value in an inline "timestamp" filter — use start/end instead.

Supported cases are v2alpha1 threshold alerts over metrics, logs, traces, or exceptions; v2alpha1 PromQL alerts; and metric-only v1 anomaly alerts, which use top-level evalWindow/frequency and no thresholds, evaluation, or schemaVersion. Before composing the payload, read signoz://alert/instructions and signoz://alert/examples; for PromQL also read signoz://promql/instructions. At least one valid notification channel is required, even when notificationSettings.usePolicy=true. Before creating, call signoz_list_notification_channels to verify user-provided names or show available names and ask the user to choose; never guess. If validation still rejects a channel name, show the current names and retry.

signoz_create_notification_channel.description:
Use this when the user wants a new SigNoz notification channel. First call signoz_list_notification_channels and confirm the requested name is not already used. Supply the provider-specific required field documented in the input schema. A test notification is sent after creation; if the test fails, the channel still exists and the response reports the failure.
SUPPORTED TYPES: slack, webhook, pagerduty, email, opsgenie, msteams

Use signoz_update_notification_channel to change an existing channel.

email_html.description: Custom HTML email template (Go template syntax supported)

email_to.description: Comma-separated list of email addresses. Required when type=email

msteams_text.description: Message body template (Go template syntax supported)

msteams_title.description: Message title template (Go template syntax supported)

msteams_webhook_url.description: MS Teams incoming webhook URL. Required when type=msteams

name.description: Unique channel name. Before creating, verify it is unused with signoz_list_notification_channels.

pagerduty_severity.description: Incident severity: critical, error, warning, or info

send_resolved.description: Whether to send notifications when alerts resolve. Default: true.

slack_api_url.description: Slack incoming webhook URL. Required when type=slack. Example: https://hooks.slack.com/services/T.../B.../xxx

slack_channel.description: Slack channel or username to post to. Example: '#alerts' or '@oncall'

slack_title.description: Message title template (Go template syntax supported)

type.description: Channel type: slack, webhook, pagerduty, email, opsgenie, or msteams.

signoz_create_view.description: Use this when the user wants to save one reusable Explorer query for Logs, Traces, Metrics, or Cost Meter; use signoz_create_dashboard for a multi-widget dashboard. Before composing any payload, you must read both signoz://view/instructions and signoz://view/examples. Cost Meter views use sourcePage="meter" while each builder spec uses signal="metrics" and source="meter". Do not send server-populated IDs or timestamps.

compositeQuery.description: The Query Builder payload as an object (not a string). Must contain queryType plus matching sub-query. See signoz://view/instructions and signoz://view/examples.

extraData.description: Optional UI-controlled options as a JSON-encoded string (safe to leave empty).

name.description: Display name of the view.

searchContext.description: Copy the user's entire original request verbatim, including any preflight or confirmation context; do not summarize, shorten, or omit clauses.

sourcePage.description: Which Explorer this view belongs to. One of: "traces", "logs", "metrics", "meter". Use "meter" for Cost Meter views (queried as metrics with source "meter").

signoz_delete_alert.description: Use this when the user explicitly wants to permanently delete a configured alert rule. Resolve its ID with signoz_list_alert_rules and confirm the exact rule first. If both steps are already complete, call this tool directly without repeating list/get preflight. Do not use it to disable a rule or clear a firing instance.

id.description: UUID of the dashboard to delete. Required; use signoz_list_dashboards to discover it.

searchContext.description: Copy the user's entire original request verbatim, including any preflight or confirmation context; do not summarize, shorten, or omit clauses.

signoz_delete_notification_channel.description: Use this when the user explicitly wants to permanently delete a notification channel. Resolve its ID with signoz_list_notification_channels and confirm the exact channel first. If both steps are already complete, call this tool directly without repeating list/get preflight. This tool does not check whether alert rules reference the channel; inspect configured rules first when dependency safety is required.

signoz_delete_view.description: Use this when the user has confirmed they want to permanently delete one saved Explorer view. The deletion is irreversible. Use signoz_list_views to discover the UUID when needed; do not use this for dashboards, which use signoz_delete_dashboard.

id.description: UUID of the saved view to delete. Required; use signoz_list_views to discover it.

signoz_get_alert.description: Use this when the user wants one configured alert rule's full definition, or before signoz_update_alert so unchanged fields can be preserved. It requires a known rule ID; use signoz_list_alert_rules to discover IDs. Do not use it for current alert instances or firing history: use signoz_list_alerts or signoz_get_alert_history.

id.description: Alert rule ID (UUIDv7 on v2 servers). Required; obtain it from signoz_list_alert_rules.

searchContext.description: Copy the user's entire original request verbatim, including any preflight or confirmation context; do not summarize, shorten, or omit clauses.

signoz_get_alert_history.description: Use this when the user wants alert firing history or the state-transition timeline of one configured rule; use signoz_list_alerts for current instances and signoz_get_alert for the rule definition. It requires a rule ID from signoz_list_alert_rules, defaults to the last 6 hours, and supports state/filter narrowing. For the next page, pass data.nextCursor as cursor and repeat the original filters, time range, and order.

cursor.description: Opaque continuation cursor. Repeat the original time range, state, filter, and order when fetching the next page. Omit cursor for the first page.

end.description: End timestamp in unix milliseconds (optional, defaults to now).

filter.description: Filter timeline labels using SigNoz query-builder syntax. Combine conditions with AND, OR, and parentheses; quote string values with single quotes and use operators such as =, !=, IN, and NOT IN. Example: "severity = 'critical' AND (team = 'payments' OR service.name = 'checkout')". To discover label keys, first call without a filter and inspect data.items[].labels[].key.name. If a filter returns no matches, retry unfiltered and verify the key spelling; malformed expressions return validation errors.

id.description: Alert rule ID. Required; obtain it from signoz_list_alert_rules.

limit.description: Rows per page. Default: 20; max: 10000 (higher values are clamped).

searchContext.description: Copy the user's entire original request verbatim, including any preflight or confirmation context; do not summarize, shorten, or omit clauses.

start.description: Start timestamp in unix milliseconds (optional, defaults to 6 hours ago).

state.description: Filter by alert state: inactive, pending, recovering, firing, nodata, or disabled. Omit to return all transitions.

timeRange.description: Relative time range. Format: <number><unit> where unit is 'm' (minutes), 'h' (hours), or 'd' (days). Examples: '30m', '1h', '2h', '6h', '24h', '3d', '7d'. Ignored when both start and end are provided. Defaults to last 6 hours if not provided.

signoz_get_dashboard.description: Use this when the user wants the complete definition of one known tenant dashboard, including its layout, variables, widgets, and queries. Use signoz_list_dashboards first when the UUID is unknown. Do not use this to browse summaries or curated templates; use signoz_list_dashboards or signoz_list_dashboard_templates respectively.

id.description: Known dashboard UUID. Required; use signoz_list_dashboards to discover it.

searchContext.description: Copy the user's entire original request verbatim, including any preflight or confirmation context; do not summarize, shorten, or omit clauses.

signoz_get_notification_channel.description: Use this when the user wants all provider-specific settings for one notification channel, especially before replacing it with signoz_update_notification_channel. It requires a known channel ID; use signoz_list_notification_channels to discover IDs. Do not use it to list channel names.

id.description: Notification channel UUID. Obtain it from signoz_list_notification_channels.

searchContext.description: Copy the user's entire original request verbatim, including any preflight or confirmation context; do not summarize, shorten, or omit clauses.

signoz_get_view.description: Use this when the user wants the complete definition of one known saved Explorer view. Use signoz_list_views first when its UUID is unknown. The returned data object is the required base for signoz_update_view because updates fully replace a view. Do not use this for multi-widget dashboards; use signoz_get_dashboard.

id.description: Saved view UUID. Use signoz_list_views to discover IDs. Required.

signoz_list_alert_rules.description: Use this when the user wants configured alert-rule summaries, including inactive/OK and disabled rules. It returns rule IDs, names, types, state, severity, labels, and timestamps; use signoz_get_alert with an ID for the full definition. Do not use it for current firing/silenced/inhibited instances: use signoz_list_alerts. Paginate with limit and offset.

limit.description: Maximum number of alert rules to return per page. Default: 50, max: 1000 (higher values are clamped).

offset.description: Number of results to skip for pagination. Default: 0.

signoz_list_alerts.description: Use this when the user wants current firing, silenced, or inhibited Alertmanager alert instances and their state, severity, timing, and rule IDs. Do not use it for configured rules or history: use signoz_list_alert_rules for rule summaries, signoz_get_alert for one definition, or signoz_get_alert_history for its timeline. Filter by alert labels, state, or receiver before paginating.

filter.description: Comma-separated alert-label comparisons; each is a label followed by =, !=, =~ (regex), or !~ (negative regex) and a quoted value. Examples: 'alertname="HighCPU"' or 'alertname="HighCPU",severity="critical"'. All comparisons must match.

limit.description: Maximum number of alerts to return per page. Default: 50, max: 1000 (higher values are clamped).

offset.description: Number of results to skip for pagination. Default: 0.

receiver.description: Regex to filter alerts by receiver name. Example: 'slack-.*' to match all Slack receivers.

signoz_list_dashboards.description: Use this when the user wants to discover tenant dashboards, browse their summaries, or find a dashboard UUID. It returns names, descriptions, tags, timestamps, and pagination metadata, not widget/query definitions; use signoz_get_dashboard for one full definition. When looking for a specific dashboard, follow pagination.nextOffset while pagination.hasMore is true before concluding it is absent.

limit.description: Maximum dashboard summaries per page. Default 50; values above 1000 are clamped.

offset.description: Number of dashboard summaries to skip. Default 0; use pagination.nextOffset for the next page.

signoz_list_notification_channels.description: Use this when the user wants to discover configured notification channels, verify exact channel names before creating or updating an alert, avoid a duplicate name before channel creation, or find a channel ID. It returns paginated summaries only: id, name, type, and timestamps; it does not return provider-specific settings. Use signoz_get_notification_channel with an ID for all settings.

limit.description: Maximum number of channels to return per page. Default: 50, max: 1000 (higher values are clamped).

offset.description: Number of results to skip before returning results. Use for pagination: offset=0 for first page, offset=50 for second page (if limit=50). Check 'pagination.nextOffset' in the response to get the next page offset. Default: 0.

searchContext.description: Copy the user's entire original request verbatim, including any preflight or confirmation context; do not summarize, shorten, or omit clauses.

signoz_list_views.description: Use this when the user wants to discover saved Explorer views or find a view UUID for one Logs, Traces, Metrics, or Cost Meter page. A view stores an Explorer query; it is not a multi-widget dashboard. Apply name/category filters before pagination, and follow pagination.nextOffset while pagination.hasMore is true before concluding a view is absent. Use signoz_get_view for one full definition.

category.description: Partial, server-side match on the saved-view category. Omit to include every category.

limit.description: Maximum number of views to return per page. Default: 50, max: 1000 (higher values are clamped).

name.description: Partial, server-side match on the saved-view name. Omit to include every name.

offset.description: Number of results to skip before returning results. Use 'pagination.nextOffset' from the previous page. Default: 0.

searchContext.description: Copy the user's entire original request verbatim, including any preflight or confirmation context; do not summarize, shorten, or omit clauses.

sourcePage.description: Explorer whose views to list: "traces", "logs", "metrics", or "meter". Use "meter" for Cost Meter, not "metrics".

signoz_update_alert.description: Use this when the user wants to change an existing SigNoz alert rule; use signoz_create_alert for a new rule. This is a full replacement: first call signoz_get_alert and merge the requested change while preserving every other field. Before composing, read signoz://alert/instructions and signoz://alert/examples; for PromQL also read signoz://promql/instructions. Before updating, call signoz_list_notification_channels to verify every selected channel name or show available names and ask the user to choose; never guess. At least one valid channel is required even when notificationSettings.usePolicy=true. If validation still rejects a channel name, show the current names and retry.

alert.description: Name of the alert rule. Must be unique and descriptive.

alertType.description: Signal type: METRIC_BASED_ALERT or LOGS_BASED_ALERT or TRACES_BASED_ALERT or EXCEPTIONS_BASED_ALERT.

annotations.description: Annotations like description and summary. Supports template variables: {{$value}} for current metric value and {{$threshold}} for the threshold and {{$labels.key}} for label values.

condition.description: Alert condition containing the query and threshold configuration.

absentFor.description: Minutes (equivalent to consecutive evaluation cycles when frequency is 1m) to wait with no data before firing an absent-data alert. Example: absentFor=15 with frequency=1m fires after 15 evaluations return no series.

alertOnAbsent.description: Alert when no data is received within the evaluation window.

algorithm.description: v1 (anomaly_rule) only. Anomaly detection algorithm; the supported value is standard (z-score based).

compositeQuery.description: The composite query defining what data to monitor.

panelType.description: Panel type. Use graph for alerts. Defaults to graph.

queries.description: Array of queries. At least one query is required.

aggregations.description: Aggregation expressions for builder queries. For metrics signal use the object shape: [{metricName: k8s.pod.cpu_request_utilization, timeAggregation: avg, spaceAggregation: max}]. For logs/traces use the expression shape: [{expression: count()}] or [{expression: p99(duration_nano)}].

expression.description: Aggregation expression (logs/traces signal). Examples: count(), avg(duration), p99(duration_nano), count_distinct(user_id), sum(bytes). Do not set metricName/timeAggregation/spaceAggregation when using this shape.

metricName.description: Metric name (metrics signal only). Example: k8s.pod.cpu_request_utilization. Use alongside timeAggregation and spaceAggregation. Do not set expression when using this shape.

spaceAggregation.description: Cross-series space aggregation (metrics signal only). Common values: sum, avg, min, max, count. For histograms use percentiles: p50, p75, p90, p95, p99.

timeAggregation.description: Per-series time aggregation (metrics signal only). Common values: avg, max, min, sum, rate, increase, count, count_distinct, latest. Default by metric type: gauge→avg, cumulative counter→rate, delta counter→sum.

expression.description: Formula expression referencing other query names (e.g. A / B * 100). Used for builder_formula type.

filter.description: Filter expression for builder queries. Example: {expression: service.name = frontend AND http.status_code >= 500}.

expression.description: Filter expression using field operators. Example: service.name = frontend AND http.status_code >= 500. Use empty string for no filter.

functions.description: Post-query functions applied to the series. Required for anomaly_rule: wrap with {name: anomaly, args: [{name: z_score_threshold, value: 2}]}.

args.description: Function arguments. Example for anomaly: [{name: z_score_threshold, value: 2}].

name.description: Argument name (e.g. z_score_threshold).

value.description: Argument value. Can be number, string, or bool depending on the function.

name.description: Function name (e.g. anomaly for ruleType=anomaly_rule).

groupBy.description: Fields to group by. Grouped dimensions appear as labels in alert notifications.

fieldContext.description: Field context: resource for resource attributes or tag for span/log attributes. Required for non-top-level fields.

fieldDataType.description: Data type of the field: string or int64 or float64 or bool.

name.description: Field name to group by (e.g. service.name or http.method or severity_text).

having.description: Having clause to filter aggregation results.

expression.description: Filter expression using field operators. Example: service.name = frontend AND http.status_code >= 500. Use empty string for no filter.

limit.description: Positive maximum number of result groups. Use 100 for standalone alert queries and formula results. Use 10000 for each builder query referenced by a formula because input limits are applied before formula evaluation.

name.description: Query name (e.g. A or B or C). Used as reference in formulas and selectedQueryName.

order.description: Query Builder v5 result order. Use __result desc for metrics and formulas; use the primary aggregation descending for logs and traces. This is the wire field order, not dashboard editor orderBy.

name.description: Field or aggregation expression to order by (e.g. timestamp or count()).

query.description: PromQL or ClickHouse SQL query string. Used when queryType is promql or clickhouse_sql. PromQL with OTel dotted metric names MUST use the Prometheus 3.x UTF-8 quoted-selector form: {"metric.name.with.dots"}. Underscored / __name__ / bare-dotted forms return no data. Read signoz://promql/instructions for the full guide (histogram patterns dotted labels pre-flight checklist).

signal.description: Signal type for builder queries: metrics or logs or traces. Required for builder_query type.

source.description: Data-source filter for metrics builder_query only. Set to meter to alert on Cost Meter (usage/billing) metrics such as signoz.meter.log.size; omit otherwise.

stepInterval.description: Step interval in seconds for time aggregation. Use 60 for metrics alerts.

type.description: Query envelope type. Must match compositeQuery.queryType: builder → builder_query or builder_formula; promql → promql; clickhouse_sql → clickhouse_sql. Also accepted: builder_trace_operator for trace operator queries.

queryType.description: Query type: builder for Query Builder or promql for PromQL or clickhouse_sql for ClickHouse SQL.

unit.description: Unit of the queried data (Y-axis unit). Used for value formatting in alert messages and for unit conversion with targetUnit in thresholds. Common values: percent, ms, s, bytes, ns, reqps, ops.

matchType.description: v1 (anomaly_rule) only. Match type - same accepted values as threshold.matchType (at_least_once, all_the_times, on_average/avg, in_total/sum, last).

op.description: v1 (anomaly_rule) only. Comparison operator applied to the anomaly score - same accepted values as threshold.op (above, below, equal, not_equal, above_or_equal, below_or_equal, outside_bounds).

name.description: Threshold tier: critical, error, warning, or info. Also used as the routing label - alerts carry threshold_name equal to this value.

op.description: Comparison operator. Canonical literals: above, below, equal, not_equal, above_or_equal, below_or_equal, outside_bounds. Short forms accepted: eq, not_eq, above_or_eq, below_or_eq. Symbolic accepted: >, <, =, !=, >=, <=. Numeric 1-7 also accepted but discouraged.

targetUnit.description: Unit of the threshold target value. If different from compositeQuery.unit the backend converts between them during evaluation. Common values: percent, ms, s, bytes, ns.

description.description: Human-readable description of what this alert monitors.

disabled.description: Whether the alert rule is disabled. Defaults to false (enabled).

Skipped entirely for anomaly_rule which uses top-level evalWindow/frequency instead.

kind.description: Evaluation kind: rolling (sliding lookback window) or cumulative (accumulates from a fixed daily/monthly reset boundary). Cumulative works for any period-total alert (e.g. daily error counts, monthly request budgets); Cost Meter spend budgets are one common use.

spec.description: Evaluation specification. For kind=rolling set evalWindow + frequency; for kind=cumulative set schedule + frequency + timezone.

evalWindow.description: Rolling kind only. Evaluation window as a Go duration string (e.g. 5m, 15m, 30m, 1h, 4h, 24h).

frequency.description: Evaluation frequency as a Go duration string (e.g. 1m, 5m, 15m).

schedule.description: Cumulative kind only. Fixed reset boundary the accumulation window starts from.

hour.description: Hour of the reset boundary (0-23); e.g. 0 for midnight.

minute.description: Minute of the reset boundary (0-59); e.g. 0 for the top of the hour.

type.description: Reset cadence: daily or monthly.

timezone.description: Cumulative kind only. IANA timezone for the schedule boundary (e.g. UTC).

frequency.description: v1 schema only (anomaly_rule). Evaluation frequency as a Go duration string (e.g. 1m, 5m, 3h). For threshold/promql rules, use evaluation.spec.frequency instead.

id.description: UUIDv7 of the alert rule to update (required). Obtain it from signoz_list_alert_rules or signoz_get_alert.

groupBy.description: Fields to group alert notifications by (e.g. service.name, k8s.namespace.name). Reduces notification noise by batching alerts with the same group key.

interval.description: Re-notification interval as a Go duration string (e.g. 15m, 30m, 1h, 4h).

query.description: PromQL query expression. For OTel metrics with dots in the name use the Prometheus 3.x UTF-8 quoted-selector form: {"metric.name.with.dots"}. Underscored / __name__ / bare-dotted forms return no data in SigNoz. Read signoz://promql/instructions for the full guide.

queryType.description: Query engine: builder, clickhouse_sql, or promql. Populate the matching sibling field and leave the other query arrays empty.

queryData.description: Frontend-only query state; the current dashboard write normalizer does not persist it. Use query for authored widgets.

queryType.description: Frontend-only query-type state; the current dashboard write normalizer does not persist it. Use query.queryType for authored widgets.

selectedLogFields.description: Columns shown by a logs list panel. Leave empty when not applicable.

dataType.description: Underlying field data type, for example string, int64, or bool.

fieldContext.description: Field namespace, such as resource or log.

fieldDataType.description: Frontend field data type when it differs from dataType.

isColumn.description: Whether the field is a materialized column.

isIndexed.description: Whether the target tenant indexes this field.

isJSON.description: Whether the field contains JSON values.

name.description: Log field name displayed as a list column.

signal.description: Signal owning the field. Use logs for selectedLogFields.

type.description: Attribute type, such as resource, tag, or log.

selectedTracesFields.description: Columns shown by a traces list panel. Leave empty when not applicable.

dataType.description: Field data type reported by SigNoz, for example string, int64, float64, or bool.

fieldContext.description: Field namespace required by selectColumns, such as resource, span, or log.

fieldDataType.description: Frontend field type required by selectColumns, for example string or int64.

id.description: Frontend attribute identifier; preserve it on update when present.

isColumn.description: Whether the field is a materialized storage column.

isJSON.description: Whether the field contains JSON values.

key.description: Attribute key used by groupBy and filters, for example service.name. Prefer key in these contexts.

name.description: Field name used by selectColumns and order entries. Prefer name in those contexts.

signal.description: Owning signal required by selectColumns: traces, logs, or metrics.

type.description: Attribute namespace reported by SigNoz, such as resource, tag, span, or log.

softMax.description: Optional soft upper display bound in yAxisUnit; it does not filter data.

softMin.description: Optional soft lower display bound in yAxisUnit; it does not filter data.

stackedBarChart.description: Whether a bar panel stacks grouped series. Default false.

thresholds.description: Visual thresholds. These color a widget; they do not create alert rules.

index.description: Stable identifier for this threshold within the widget.

isEditEnabled.description: Frontend edit state; normally false or omitted.

keyIndex.description: Frontend ordering index for this threshold.

selectedGraph.description: Query or series the threshold applies to; preserve it when updating an existing threshold.

thresholdFormat.description: How the threshold is rendered. Allowed values: 'Text' or 'Background'. SigNoz does NOT support a Grafana-style 'Line' marker; do not use 'Line'. 'Background' tints the panel area when the operator+value condition holds; 'Text' colors the threshold value label only.

thresholdLabel.description: Optional display label for the threshold.

thresholdTableOptions.description: Table threshold display option; preserve the value returned by signoz_get_dashboard.

thresholdUnit.description: Unit for the threshold value (should match the panel's yAxisUnit).

thresholdValue.description: Numeric value the operator is compared against.

timePreferance.description: Time range mode. Use GLOBAL_TIME; this intentionally matches the frontend's timePreferance spelling and defaults to GLOBAL_TIME.

title.description: Widget title displayed on the dashboard.

yAxisUnit.description: SigNoz unit identifier for values and the y-axis, for example ms, s, bytes, percentunit, or none.

id.description: Dashboard UUID to update (required).

searchContext.description: Copy the user's entire original request verbatim, including any preflight or confirmation context; do not summarize, shorten, or omit clauses.

signoz_update_notification_channel.description:
Use this when the user wants to change an existing SigNoz notification channel. This is a full replacement: first find the ID with signoz_list_notification_channels, then call signoz_get_notification_channel and merge the requested change while preserving the complete provider configuration and send_resolved value. Omitting send_resolved resets it to true. A test notification is sent after update; an update can succeed even when that test fails, which is reported in the response.
SUPPORTED TYPES: slack, webhook, pagerduty, email, opsgenie, msteams

Do not use this for partial updates.

email_html.description: Custom HTML email template (Go template syntax supported)

email_to.description: Comma-separated list of email addresses. Required when type=email

id.description: Notification channel UUID. Obtain it from signoz_list_notification_channels.

msteams_text.description: Message body template (Go template syntax supported)

msteams_title.description: Message title template (Go template syntax supported)

msteams_webhook_url.description: MS Teams incoming webhook URL. Required when type=msteams

name.description: Complete replacement channel name. Preserve the current name unless the user requested a change.

opsgenie_api_key.description: OpsGenie API key. Required when type=opsgenie

opsgenie_priority.description: Alert priority: P1, P2, P3, P4, or P5

pagerduty_routing_key.description: PagerDuty integration/routing key. Required when type=pagerduty

pagerduty_severity.description: Incident severity: critical, error, warning, or info

searchContext.description: Copy the user's entire original request verbatim, including any preflight or confirmation context; do not summarize, shorten, or omit clauses.

send_resolved.description: Complete replacement resolved-notification setting. Copy the current value from signoz_get_notification_channel unless changing it; omission resets to true.

slack_api_url.description: Slack incoming webhook URL. Required when type=slack. Example: https://hooks.slack.com/services/T.../B.../xxx

slack_channel.description: Slack channel or username to post to. Example: '#alerts' or '@oncall'

slack_text.description: Message body template (Go template syntax supported)

slack_title.description: Message title template (Go template syntax supported)

type.description: Complete replacement channel type: slack, webhook, pagerduty, email, opsgenie, or msteams. Preserve the current type unless the user requested a change.

webhook_url.description: Webhook endpoint URL. Required when type=webhook

signoz_update_view.description: Use this when the user wants to change an existing saved Explorer view. This is a full replacement: call signoz_get_view first, modify its data object, preserve every unrequested field, and pass that full object as view. Read signoz://view/instructions and signoz://view/examples when changing sourcePage or compositeQuery; skip them for name-, category-, or tags-only changes when you already have the complete fetched view. Keep the UUID only in id; omit server-populated IDs and timestamps from view.

id.description: UUID of the view to replace. Required.

searchContext.description: Copy the user's entire original request verbatim, including any preflight or confirmation context; do not summarize, shorten, or omit clauses.

view.description: Complete saved view after the requested changes. Start with the data returned by signoz_get_view and pass the full object here.

compositeQuery.description: The Query Builder payload as an object (not a string). Must contain queryType plus matching sub-query. See signoz://view/instructions and signoz://view/examples.

extraData.description: Optional UI-controlled options as a JSON-encoded string (safe to leave empty).

name.description: Display name of the view.

sourcePage.description: Which Explorer this view belongs to. One of: "traces", "logs", "metrics", "meter". Use "meter" for Cost Meter views (queried as metrics with source "meter").
